root_idea.summary: A root centered on kindling: ignition, burning, blazing, and rising in heat or intensity.
root_idea.development: From the literal kindling and intensification of fire, the root extends to heat, spreading or inflamed activity, madness, contagion, vehement motion, and the rising or fixing of prices.

qac_form_accounting.reason: A distinct Quran-attested Form II passive verb meaning to be set ablaze.
A distinct Quran-attested nominal referring to blazing fire.
A distinct Quran-attested nominal with Quranic interpretations including madness and distress or punishment.

senses.definition: To kindle, set ablaze, or make burn fiercely.
senses.usage_conditions: Quranically attested in the passive feminine perfect, describing the blazing of the Fire; the doubled Form II can carry an intensive force.

senses.definition: A kindled, blazing fire; the fire or flame itself when blazing.
senses.usage_conditions: Used substantively for the blazing fire, especially the eschatological fire and its punishment; the form is also explained as a فعيل form carrying the sense of مفعول, “kindled.”
A Quranic interpretation of سُعُر in the expression occurring in al-Qamar 54:24 and 54:47.
An alternative Quranic interpretation of the same expression; some explanations connect the distress or punishment with the error that occasions it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To kindle or inflame war.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of kindling fire, used with war as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To excite or inflame people against one another or against a group.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative causative use with people, evil, or mischief as the provoking force.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To inflict extensive evil or mischief on people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic figurative construction distinct from merely exciting or inflaming them.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To burn or painfully wound with arrows.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or intensified description of the pain caused by shooting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To communicate mange or scab to other animals; the transmission of a contagious disease.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the spread of mange, scab, or another disease from one animal or person to another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be struck by the hot wind called samūm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive or stative use describing a person affected by intense hot wind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become vehemently hungry and thirsty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes an intense, burning state of hunger or thirst.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become mad, insane, or possessed by a demon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A non-Quranic lexical use of the verb distinct from the Quranic noun interpretation of سُعُر.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a circuit in pursuit of an objective; to go around or practice circumvention.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic use describing purposeful circuiting or comparable circumvention.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To travel throughout the night with riding camels or other beasts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of sustained night travel with mounts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a she-camel to be quick or swift in going.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical use specifically describing the speed of a she-camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To assign, declare, or agree upon a price or rate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used for fixing a known price, announcing the current selling rate, a governor’s price regulation, or agreement on a selling price.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To act with someone or something as though mad, like a mad dog.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An expressly figurative Form III use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To excite or annoy by leaping or bounding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a wild animal whose leaping provokes or disturbs others.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a fire to burn, blaze, flame, or burn fiercely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form VIII use describing fire itself becoming ablaze.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For war or evil to rage or spread.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative intransitive use modeled on fire spreading.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For thieves or robbers to set themselves in motion for mischief.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use portraying their activity as though they had caught fire.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For mange or scab to begin and spread in a camel’s vulnerable body regions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the onset or spread of mange in the armpits, groins, lips, or similar parts of a camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For people to move in every direction gathering and eating fresh ripe dates.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized figurative use describing widespread, vigorous movement to obtain dates.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vehement, rapid, or burning-painful shooting or throwing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression for shooting with extraordinary force or speed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Vehement hunger, thirst, or burning desire for food.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence distinguishes intense hunger or thirst from the Quranic interpretation of سُعُر as madness or distress.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The current price or selling rate of a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: By idiom, something may be said to have a price when it is highly valuable, or to have no price when it is extremely cheap.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Mad, insane, or possessed by a demon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective describing a person; the cited animal application is treated separately below.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Restless or unable to remain still, especially of a she-camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence connects this animal adjective with the idea of madness or excessive agitation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cough, especially a sharp cough.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An archaic nominal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The beginning or newness of an affair or case.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Refers to the onset or freshness of a matter, not to a cough.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A color inclining to blackness, somewhat darker than admah.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A color term applied to complexion or other coloration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Vehemence of running.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun of intensity describing forceful or rapid motion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Daybreak.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use for the onset of daylight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rays of sunlight entering an aperture, or the motes visible moving in those rays.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression can refer either to the beams or to particles seen within them.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The heat of fire, and figuratively the heat of night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A heat noun extended from the burning heat of fire.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Evil or mischief that causes disturbance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic figurative use describing destructive agitation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel that is quick or swift in going.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal adjective or noun of description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular idol belonging to the tribe of ʿAnazah.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proper cultic designation, distinct from the common noun سَعِير.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fire-place or oven dug in the ground for baking bread.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical object noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The chief of the Christians in knowledge of medicine and its instruments.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical title reported as originally deriving from a Syriac term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having a complexion of the color called suʿrah.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective applied to a man; the corresponding feminine form is reported separately in the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lean, lank, slender, or emaciated, with little flesh and visible sinews.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective describing bodily leanness or a gaunt appearance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The slender part of a camel’s tail.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical animal term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tool, stick, or iron instrument used to stir or intensify a fire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural forms are reported as مساعر and مساعير.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who makes the fire of war rage; a stirrer of war.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative occupational or character description derived from the fire-stirring tool.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Long or strong.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use applied to a neck or another thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Mad, when applied to a dog.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal adjective linked with excessive agitation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse whose legs are thrown apart in its movement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of a horse’s gait, especially movement without a compact gathered leap.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man struck by the hot wind called samūm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial description of someone affected by hot wind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Vehemently hungry or thirsty; intensely eager for food or drink.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes burning appetite, even when the belly is full.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The armpits, groins or similar parts, and lips of camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized plural anatomical term associated with places where mange begins or becomes severe.

cautions: The Quranic noun سُعُر in 54:24 and 54:47 has competing classical interpretations; both madness and distress or punishment are recorded rather than reduced to the contextual gloss alone.

The Quranic Form II verb is attested in a passive inflected form, but the public headword is normalized to the dictionary citation form سَعَّرَ. The Quranic reading tradition also includes a non-doubled form.
